---
title: "Options"
subtitle: "Every totalme option, with an example of each"
---

```stata
totalme varlist [if] [in] [, options]
```

The examples use Stata's `nlsw88` data with occupation collapsed to three
groups and modeled with `mlogit`.

```{.stata-run}
. sysuse nlsw88, clear
(NLSW, 1988 extract)

. drop if missing(occupation, wage, ttl_exp)
(9 observations deleted)

. recode occupation (1/2 = 1 "Professional/managerial") (3/5 = 2 "Sales/clerical/craft") ///
>                   (6/13 = 3 "Other"), gen(occ3)
(1,920 differences between occupation and occ3)

. 
. quietly mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south, vce(robust)

. estimates store basemod

. quietly mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)

. estimates store medmod

```

## `models()` -- one model or two

`models()` is optional for one model (the estimates in memory are used) and
required for two. With two models the Total ME is reported for each and the
difference is tested; the two models can be the same or different estimation
commands. `vce(robust)` is strongly recommended on both.

```{.stata-run}
. totalme collgrad age, models(medmod)
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad age

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad                 |                                               
College grad vs Not co~d |      0.264       0.023      11.527       0.000 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age                      |                                               
          + 1 (centered) |      0.007       0.003       2.267       0.023 

. totalme collgrad age, models(basemod medmod)


Model 1 (basemod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south
Model 2 (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad age

Total ME Estimates (N_basemod = 2237 , N_medmod = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Model 1 (basemod) |      0.248       0.021      11.572       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
        Model 2 (medmod) |      0.264       0.023      11.527       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Cross-Model Diff. |     -0.016       0.008      -2.049       0.040 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age, + 1 (centered)      |                                               
       Model 1 (basemod) |      0.005       0.003       1.831       0.067 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age, + 1 (centered)      |                                               
        Model 2 (medmod) |      0.007       0.003       2.267       0.023 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age, + 1 (centered)      |                                               
       Cross-Model Diff. |     -0.001       0.001      -1.152       0.249 

```

## `amount()`, `centered`, `uncentered` -- the size of a continuous change

For a continuous variable the default is a one-unit change, centered on the
observed value. `amount()` takes a number or `sd`; one value applies to all
continuous variables, several apply in order. `uncentered` makes the change
run upward from the observed value.

```{.stata-run}
. totalme age, models(medmod) amount(sd)
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     age

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age                      |                                               
         + SD (centered) |      0.020       0.009       2.268       0.023 

. totalme age, models(medmod) amount(10) uncentered
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     age

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age                      |                                               
                    + 10 |      0.060       0.024       2.494       0.013 

```

## `start()` -- where the change begins

```{.stata-run}
. totalme age, models(medmod) start(age=35) amount(10)
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     age
1

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
age                      |                                               
start (35) + 10 (cente~) |      0.069       0.032       2.140       0.032 

```

## `weighted`, `unweighted`, `all` -- nominal variables

For a nominal variable the per-outcome quantity is the ME inequality of
[`meinequality`](../meinequality/index.html), so the Total ME is a Total ME
inequality, weighted by category shares by default. `unweighted` gives every
pairwise comparison the same weight; `all` reports both.

```{.stata-run}
. totalme race, models(medmod)
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Nominal IV(s):
     race

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
race                     |                                               
          total ME Ineq. |      0.147       0.043       3.427       0.001 

. totalme race, models(medmod) unweighted
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Nominal IV(s):
     race

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
race                     |                                               
    Unwgt total ME Ineq. |      0.149       0.051       2.922       0.003 

. totalme race, models(medmod) all
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Nominal IV(s):
     race

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
race                     |                                               
          total ME Ineq. |      0.147       0.043       3.427       0.001 
    Unwgt total ME Ineq. |      0.149       0.051       2.922       0.003 

```

## `groups` and `groupnames()` -- models fit on distinct samples

```{.stata-run}
. quietly mlogit occ3 i.collgrad c.age if south == 0, vce(robust)

. estimates store nonsouth

. quietly mlogit occ3 i.collgrad c.age if south == 1, vce(robust)

. estimates store south

. 
. totalme collgrad, models(nonsouth south) groups groupnames(NonSouth South)


Model 1 (nonsouth) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad c.age if south == 0
Model 2 (south) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad c.age if south == 1
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad

Total ME Estimates (N_nonsouth = 1300 , N_south = 937)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
      Model 1 (NonSouth) |      0.277       0.028       9.886       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
         Model 2 (South) |      0.228       0.036       6.292       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Cross-Model Diff. |      0.049       0.046       1.079       0.281 

```

## `by()` and `over()` -- within levels of another variable

`by(varname)` computes the Total ME at each level of a binary or nominal
covariate as a counterfactual (the whole sample set to that level);
`over(varname)` computes it within each observed subgroup. The variable must
be in the model with the `i.` prefix.

```{.stata-run}
. totalme collgrad, models(medmod) by(south)
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad(Not south)      |                                               
College grad vs Not co~d |      0.272       0.024      11.451       0.000 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad(South)          |                                               
College grad vs Not co~d |      0.254       0.023      11.130       0.000 

. totalme collgrad, models(medmod) over(south)
Model (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage, vce(robust)
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad

Total ME Estimates (N = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad(Not south)      |                                               
College grad vs Not co~d |      0.275       0.024      11.261       0.000 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad(South)          |                                               
College grad vs Not co~d |      0.248       0.022      11.398       0.000 

```

## `commands` and `details`

`commands` prints the `margins` command (and with two models the `suest2`
command) that produced the estimates; `details` prints their output.

```{.stata-run}
. totalme collgrad, models(basemod medmod) commands


Model 1 (basemod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south
Model 2 (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage
suest2 model is: 
     suest2 basemod medmod
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad
margins specification is: 
     margins , at(collgrad=(0 1))    post

Total ME Estimates (N_basemod = 2237 , N_medmod = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Model 1 (basemod) |      0.248       0.021      11.572       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
        Model 2 (medmod) |      0.264       0.023      11.527       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Cross-Model Diff. |     -0.016       0.008      -2.049       0.040 

```

## Weights, svy, and mi

Weights, the `svy:` prefix, and `mi estimate` go on the stored models, not
on `totalme`; with two models both must carry the same. Multilevel models
need a higher-level weight as well or, better, the `svy:` prefix. See the
[help file](help.html#sampleweights).

## Saved results

`totalme` is r-class. For a continuous or binary variable, `r(tmcm1#)`,
`r(tmcm2#)`, and `r(tmcd#)` hold the Total ME for model 1, model 2, and their
difference for the *#*th such variable in *varlist*; for a nominal variable
`r(tmwm1#)`, `r(tmwm2#)`, `r(tmwd#)` hold the weighted Total ME inequality and
`r(tmuwm1#)`, `r(tmuwm2#)`, `r(tmuwd#)` the unweighted. With `by()` or
`over()`, `_level` is appended. `r(table)` holds the displayed table and
`r(se_missing)` counts quantities whose standard error could not be computed.
The `margins` results are stored as `totalme_margins` and, with two models,
the combined system as `totalme_suest2`.

```{.stata-run}
. totalme collgrad race, models(basemod medmod)


Model 1 (basemod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south
Model 2 (medmod) is:
     mlogit occ3 i.collgrad i.race c.age i.south c.ttl_exp c.wage
Continuous/Binary IV(s): 
     collgrad
Nominal IV(s):
     race

Total ME Estimates (N_basemod = 2237 , N_medmod = 2237)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Model 1 (basemod) |      0.248       0.021      11.572       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
        Model 2 (medmod) |      0.264       0.023      11.527       0.000 
collgrad,College grad ~l |                                               
       Cross-Model Diff. |     -0.016       0.008      -2.049       0.040 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
race total ME Ineq.      |                                               
       Model 1 (basemod) |      0.152       0.044       3.492       0.000 
        Model 2 (medmod) |      0.147       0.043       3.427       0.001 
       Cross-Model Diff. |      0.005       0.006       0.902       0.367 

. return list

scalars:
         r(se_missing) =  0
              r(tmwd1) =  .0053498747963924
             r(tmwm21) =  .1469832421949591
             r(tmwm11) =  .1523331169913515
              r(tmcd1) =  -.0160303373827734
             r(tmcm21) =  .2637991970588639
             r(tmcm11) =  .2477688596760905
             r(n_vars) =  2
             r(n_mods) =  2

matrices:
              r(table) :  6 x 6

```

## Bootstrap standard errors

```stata
capture program drop boot_tot
program define boot_tot, rclass
    mlogit healthR i.race4 c.age i.woman, base(1)
    totalme race4
    return scalar w_tot = r(tmwm11)
end

bootstrap w_tot=r(w_tot), reps(1000): boot_tot
```
